Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

today adverb and noun

this day

also this day, today’s, before today, starting today, from today

classical

Ter. Eun. 697: Quandō? — Hodiē.
Cic. Att. 13.30.2: negat … hodiē: crās māne putat (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 89, 395

hodiē

adverb · Wiktionary

From hōc diē. With a time of day: hodiē māne, this morning; hodiē vesperī, this evening (see those).

Other words

  • hodiernus, hodierna, hodiernum — today’s, of today

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Cat. 3.21: hodiernō diē (Lewis & Short); Gell. 15.7.3: quālis est hodiernus · Declension on Wiktionary

Examples

  • subitō nōbīs hodiē Alexandrīnae nāvēs appāruērunt

    suddenly today the ships from Alexandria came into sightSen. Ep. 77.1

  • sed properā, nec tē ventūrās differ in hōrās; quī nōn est hodiē, crās minus aptus erit

    but hurry, and don’t put yourself off to the hours to come: whoever isn’t ready today will be less so tomorrowOv. Rem. 93–94

  • ante hunc diem

    before todayTraupman 89

  • ex hōc diē

    starting todayTraupman 89

See also today, yesterday, tomorrow, this morning, this evening, what did you do today?, what’s the date?.
